fields.summary: User can reset their password via an emailed link
fields.description:
As a registered user I want to reset my password through a link sent to my email so that I can regain access when I forget it.

Project Key: SMOKE
Issue ID (numeric): 10001

Acceptance Criteria:
1. A 'Forgot password' link on the login page opens a form that accepts an email address.
2. Submitting a registered email sends a password-reset link that expires after 60 minutes.
3. Submitting an unregistered email shows the same confirmation message (no account enumeration).
4. Opening a valid link lets the user set a new password that must meet the complexity policy.
5. An expired or already-used link shows an error and offers to request a new one.

review_comments:
h3. Requirements review: SMOKE-1

The five acceptance criteria cover the main flow and are largely testable, but four leave the observable
outcome open and the attached reset policy adds a rule none of them mention.

*Findings*
# The attached reset-policy.txt caps reset requests at 3 per account per hour, but no criterion covers
it: the behaviour of the 4th request within an hour is undefined.
# AC 3 requires the same confirmation message for an unregistered address, but not the same status code
or response time. Either difference re-introduces the account enumeration the criterion exists to prevent.
# AC 4 refers to "the complexity policy" without naming or restating it, so it cannot be turned into a
test with a definite outcome.
# AC 5 covers an expired or already-used link, yet the story never says whether the link is single-use,
nor whether requesting a new one invalidates the previous one.
# The attachment reset-request.json carries a locale, but no criterion states the reset email is sent in it.

*Missing*: nothing describes what happens to active sessions on other devices after a successful reset.

*Suggestion*: add criteria for the rate limit, the single-use guarantee and the complexity rules, and
restate AC 3 as "the response is indistinguishable for registered and unregistered addresses".

test_cases.name: Forgot password link opens the email entry form
test_cases.objective: Verify that the login page offers a 'Forgot password' entry point that leads to a form accepting an email address.
test_cases.precondition: The login page is reachable and the user is not authenticated.
test_cases.review_comments: Covers AC 1 end to end. Add an assertion that the form is reachable by keyboard, since it is the only entry point to the flow.

steps.description: Open the login page as an unauthenticated user.
steps.expected_result: The login page is displayed with a 'Forgot password' link.
A form with a single email address field and a submit button is displayed.
The email field accepts an email address and is the only required input.

test_cases.name: Reset link is emailed for a registered address
test_cases.objective: Verify that submitting a registered email address sends a password-reset link to that address.
test_cases.precondition: A user account exists for registered@example.com and the mailbox is observable.
test_cases.review_comments: Good coverage of AC 2. Assert on the recipient of the email as well, so a reset link sent to the wrong address cannot pass.

steps.description: Submit registered@example.com in the 'Forgot password' form.
steps.expected_result: The request is accepted and a confirmation message is displayed.
Exactly one password-reset email addressed to registered@example.com has arrived.

steps.description: Open the reset link from the email.

test_cases.name: Reset link expires 60 minutes after it was issued
test_cases.objective: Verify that a reset link is rejected once its 60-minute validity from the reset policy has elapsed.
test_cases.precondition: A reset link has been requested for registered@example.com and its issuing time is known.
test_cases.review_comments: The boundary is the valuable part here. State explicitly whether 60 minutes exactly is still valid, so the step at the boundary has one unambiguous outcome.

steps.description: Request a reset link for registered@example.com and record the time it was issued.
steps.expected_result: The reset email arrives and the link is valid.

steps.description: Open the link 59 minutes after it was issued.
Open the link 61 minutes after it was issued.
steps.expected_result: The link is rejected with an expiry error and no password form is shown.

test_cases.name: Unregistered address gets the same confirmation as a registered one
test_cases.objective: Verify that the response to an unregistered email address is indistinguishable from the response to a registered one, so accounts cannot be enumerated.
test_cases.precondition: no-account@example.com has no user account; registered@example.com has one.
test_cases.review_comments: Directly covers AC 3. Compare the HTTP status and the response body of both submissions, not only the visible message, otherwise enumeration through the status code still passes.

steps.description: Submit registered@example.com in the 'Forgot password' form and record the response.
steps.expected_result: A confirmation message is displayed and the response status is recorded.

steps.description: Submit no-account@example.com in the same form and record the response.
steps.expected_result: The same confirmation message is displayed with the same response status.

test_cases.name: New password must satisfy the complexity policy
test_cases.objective: Verify that the set-new-password form rejects a password violating the complexity policy and accepts a compliant one.
test_cases.precondition: A valid, unused reset link for registered@example.com is available.
test_cases.review_comments: Covers AC 4, but the policy it asserts against is not defined in the story; pin the expected rules in the test data once the requirement names them.

steps.description: Open the valid reset link and submit the password 'test'.
steps.expected_result: The password is rejected with a message naming the unmet complexity rules.

steps.description: Submit a password meeting the complexity policy.
steps.expected_result: The password is accepted and a confirmation is displayed.

steps.description: Log in with the new password.
steps.expected_result: The user is authenticated and reaches the account home page.

test_cases.name: Used or expired link is rejected and a new one can be requested
test_cases.objective: Verify that a reset link cannot be used twice and that the rejection offers a way to request a new link.
test_cases.precondition: A reset password flow has been completed once with a valid link for registered@example.com.
test_cases.review_comments: Covers AC 5 including the recovery path. Also assert that the newly requested link works, so the offer is not merely cosmetic.

steps.description: Complete the password reset with a valid link.
steps.expected_result: The password is changed and a confirmation is displayed.

steps.description: Open the same reset link a second time.
steps.expected_result: The link is rejected with an error stating it has already been used.

steps.description: Follow the offer to request a new reset link.
steps.expected_result: A new reset email arrives for registered@example.com.

bugs.summary: Password reset request for a registered address returns HTTP 500 and queues no email
bugs.description:
*Steps to reproduce*
# Send POST /api/password-reset with the body {"email": "registered@example.com", "locale": "en-GB"}.
# Observe the response status and body.
# Inspect the outgoing mail queue for that address.

*Expected result*
HTTP 200 and a password-reset email queued for registered@example.com, as acceptance criterion 2 of
SMOKE-1 requires.

*Actual result*
HTTP 500 with an empty body, and nothing reached the mail queue, so a registered user cannot recover
their account through the emailed link at all.

*Environment*
Smoke Test Environment, executed by the agent 'Smoke API Test Executor', version 9.9-smoke.

*Traceability*
Story SMOKE-1, test case SMOKE-T100. The request never reaches the mail queue, which points at the reset
endpoint rather than at the mail transport.
